newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss ABB sees no 1997 uptrend.
newsitem.headline: Swiss ABB sees no 1997 uptrend.

text.p: ABB Switzerland, part of the ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG electrical engineering group, said it does not expect a significant uptrend this year given the global market and competitive environment.
"Given the global market and competitive environment ABB Switzerland does not expect a significant uptrend during the current year," ABB said in a statement.

In 1996 ABB Switzerland's net profit fell to 248 million Swiss francs from 384 million, but a comparison between the two years is not conclusive because 1996 results do not include the proceeds from the segregation of ABB's Transportation Systems nor its net income.
Business in 1996 was characterised by sluggish markets in the industrialised nations and fierce price competition in the power generation sector worldwide.
Despite the rise in global power consumption, privatisation has caused an erosion in the prices of power generation systems.
Conversely, business with services as well as power plant maintenance and operation was reassuring, ABB said.

ABB Switzerland intends to further strengthen its presence in Asia and Latin America and sees encouraging perspectives with its technologies in gas turbines and combined-cycle power plants. It also expects its market share in hydro power plants to continue to grow.
ABB Switzerland's 1996 orders fell nine percent to 4.472 billion francs, reflecting the depressed power plant business. Revenue was slightly down to 5.066 billion francs from 5.141 billion.
Pre-tax profit in 1996 was 34 percent below 1995 at 301 million, but excluding the higher-than-normal unusual items in 1995, pre-tax profit would have been down 21 percent.

ABB Switzerland's workforce fell to 10,500 from 12,700 due to the sale of the Transportation Systems -- which was merged with Daimler-Benz AG's transportation activities into ADtranz -- and the transformation of the apprenticeship training organisation into an independent entity.

Within the Power Transmission and Distribution division, ABB said price pressure had mounted perceptibly and uncertainties in conjuntion with the deregulation trend in the utilities sector has resulted in a more cautious investment behavior.
